prompt.context_jp: 幼稚園のカナリヤ組の教室には、朝から子供たちのにぎやかな声___響いていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 幼稚園のカナリヤ組の教室には、朝から子供たちのにぎやかな声___響いていた。

feedback.correct_en: The cheerful voices are newly introduced into the scene as the sound that fills the classroom — new information presented as part of a scene description, so が is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would mark 'the voices' as a known topic being contrasted or commented on, but here the narrator is painting a scene, not resuming an old topic.

contrast_examples.en: Children's voices can be heard. (new info)
Those voices (we already know of) were loud. (topic)

prompt.context_jp: 担任の冴子先生___前に立ち、手を叩いてみんなの注意を集める。
prompt.prompt_jp: 担任の冴子先生___前に立ち、手を叩いてみんなの注意を集める。

feedback.correct_en: Saeko-sensei is being newly introduced into the scene as the actor doing the standing and clapping; が marks this new participant.
feedback.incorrect_en: を would make her a direct object, and に would mark a destination — neither fits as the subject of 立ち.

prompt.context_jp: 仕事が低迷して家にいる時間ばかり___増えた和之にとって…
prompt.prompt_jp: 仕事が低迷して家にいる時間ばかり___増えた和之にとって…

feedback.correct_en: Inside a relative clause modifying 和之, が marks the subject of 増えた. Clause-internal subjects typically take が, not は.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would try to set 'time at home' as a topic, but this is a subordinate clause describing Kazuyuki; a topic marker wouldn't fit here.

contrast_examples.en: a person whose time has increased
As for time, it has increased. (main clause topic)

prompt.context_jp: 一方の理絵___、すでに役になりきった顔つきで、見えない籠を両手に抱えている。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一方の理絵___、すでに役になりきった顔つきで、見えない籠を両手に抱えている。

feedback.correct_en: 一方の (on the other hand) sets up a contrast with Kazuyuki in the previous sentence. Contrastive topic は is the natural choice.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce Rie as new information, but she's already in the scene; the sentence is contrasting her attitude with her father's.

contrast_examples.jp: 父は台本を読み、娘は演じていた。
contrast_examples.en: The father read the script; the daughter, on the other hand, was acting.

prompt.context_jp: 継母の台詞___、和之は台本から目を離さずに棒読みしていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 継母の台詞___、和之は台本から目を離さずに棒読みしていた。

feedback.correct_en: 棒読みする takes a direct object — the thing being read monotonously. 台詞 is what Kazuyuki is reading, so を is correct.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark the lines as subject (they aren't doing anything), and は would try to topicalize them, but the sentence already has 和之は as topic.

prompt.context_jp: 玄関から聞こえた母親の声に、理絵___台本を放り出して駆けていった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 玄関から聞こえた母親の声に、理絵___台本を放り出して駆けていった。

feedback.correct_en: Rie is the established topic of this scene. The sentence tells us what she does in reaction, so topic-marker は fits naturally.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would reintroduce Rie as if she were new to the scene, but she has been the focus throughout the practice.

contrast_examples.jp: 誰かが来た。理絵が入ってきた。
contrast_examples.en: Someone came. Rie came in. (new participant)

prompt.context_jp: 和之の何気ない言葉に、美紀___箸を持つ手を止めた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 和之の何気ない言葉に、美紀___箸を持つ手を止めた。

feedback.correct_en: Miki is the viewpoint character of this passage. The narrator describes her reaction to the husband's words, so topic-は fits.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would present Miki as newly noticed; を is ungrammatical since 手を already appears as the object.

prompt.context_jp: 一方の和之___、何かを思い出そうとするように天井を見上げていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 一方の和之___、何かを思い出そうとするように天井を見上げていた。

feedback.correct_en: '一方の' explicitly signals a contrast with Miki, who is deep in thought. Contrastive は naturally pairs with 一方.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce Kazuyuki as new information, but the whole point is to contrast his obliviousness with Miki's inner turmoil.

contrast_examples.jp: 妻は悩み、一方の夫はのんきだった。
contrast_examples.en: The wife worried; the husband, by contrast, was carefree.
(It was) the husband who was carefree.

prompt.context_jp: 冴子の手___、ふと止まった。
prompt.prompt_jp: 冴子の手___、ふと止まった。

feedback.correct_en: This is a sudden event description — the narrator notices her hand stopping. Such presentational, scene-reporting sentences take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would make 'her hand' a topic for comment, flattening the surprise. The 'ふと' (suddenly) cue pairs with event-marking が.

contrast_examples.en: The door is open. (describing a state)

prompt.context_jp: 「お遊びに見えるかもしれないけど― 私にとって___大事な仕事なんだから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「お遊びに見えるかもしれないけど― 私にとって___大事な仕事なんだから」

feedback.correct_en: Saeko is contrasting 'to you it may look like play, but for ME it's important work.' Contrastive は after にとって emphasizes her perspective.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would awkwardly re-mark 私にとって as a subject, but the frame 'for me' is being contrasted with how others see it — that's classic contrastive は.

contrast_examples.jp: 君には遊びでも、私には仕事だ。
contrast_examples.en: To you it's play, but to me it's work.

prompt.context_jp: 「なんでだろ？ あなたの子供な___に」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「なんでだろ？ あなたの子供な___に」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the correct particle (the one before に).

feedback.correct_en: のに is a conjunction meaning 'even though.' Shoko is teasingly wondering why their son is so shy despite being Yusuke's child.
feedback.incorrect_en: 'がに' is not a valid construction; this is the concessive のに connecting clauses.

contrast_examples.en: Even though I'm young, I get tired.

prompt.context_jp: 運ばれてきた料理を前に、美紀___フォークを持ったまま、しばらく皿を見つめていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 運ばれてきた料理を前に、美紀___フォークを持ったまま、しばらく皿を見つめていた。

feedback.correct_en: Miki is the continuing topic of this passage about her dinner with Shoko. は marks her as the ongoing subject the narrator is commenting on.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would introduce Miki as a brand-new participant, but she's already the focus of the scene.

prompt.context_jp: かぜが治りきらない理絵___、和之は結局幼稚園まで連れてくる羽目になった。
prompt.prompt_jp: かぜが治りきらない理絵___、和之は結局幼稚園まで連れてくる羽目になった。

feedback.correct_en: 連れてくる takes Rie as its direct object — Kazuyuki brings her along. を marks that object, fronted to the start for emphasis.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would mark her as subject (she isn't doing the bringing), and に would mark her as a destination or indirect object, which doesn't fit.

contrast_examples.jp: 子供を幼稚園に連れていく。

prompt.context_jp: 「あの… 私___書いたんですけど 何か問題でも？」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「あの… 私___書いたんですけど 何か問題でも？」

feedback.correct_en: Kazuyuki asked who wrote the script. Saeko is identifying herself as the specific writer — this is exhaustive-listing が ('it was I who wrote it').
feedback.incorrect_en: '私は書いた' would merely report what she did as a topic, not answer the 'who' question. In response to 誰が…? the answer takes が.

contrast_examples.en: I'm the one who wrote it.
As for me, I wrote it. (reporting about myself)

prompt.context_jp: 机の上の携帯電話___、短く震えた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 机の上の携帯電話___、短く震えた。

feedback.correct_en: A sudden event is being presented — the phone unexpectedly vibrates. Event/presentational sentences take が.
feedback.incorrect_en: は would topicalize the phone as if commenting on its properties, but this line is reporting a new happening that moves the plot.

contrast_examples.en: As for the phone, it's old. (comment)

prompt.context_jp: 美紀___しばらく黙ったまま、何かを考えていた。
prompt.prompt_jp: 美紀___しばらく黙ったまま、何かを考えていた。

feedback.correct_en: Miki continues as the viewpoint character across several sentences describing her inner thoughts. Topic-は is natural.
feedback.incorrect_en: が would reintroduce her as new to the scene, which doesn't match the continuous inner monologue following.

prompt.context_jp: 「決まらないままなら― 君にずっと___もらえるなあ」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「決まらないままなら― 君にずっと___もらえるなあ」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose the word that fits the boss's joking remark.

feedback.correct_en: Ueda is joking that if Miki's husband never finds a job, he can keep her working at the company. 働いてもらえる is the natural collocation.
feedback.incorrect_en: 遊んで or 休んで would reverse the meaning — a boss wouldn't joke about his employee playing or resting indefinitely.

contrast_examples.jp: ずっと働いてもらいたい。
contrast_examples.en: I'd like you to keep working (for us).
I want to keep playing forever.

prompt.context_jp: 「___が痛いです」(when someone points out a painful truth about you)
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___が痛いです」
prompt.prompt_en: Which word completes this idiom meaning 'that hits home / painful to hear'?

feedback.correct_en: 耳が痛い literally 'my ears hurt' is a fixed idiom meaning the criticism is uncomfortably true. Miki uses it when the boss remarks that couples rarely talk things through.
feedback.incorrect_en: 目が痛い and 口が痛い are not idiomatic for 'the truth hurts'; 目が痛い just means literal eye pain.

contrast_examples.en: That's a hard truth to hear.

prompt.context_jp: 「___働きかよ」(complaining that there's no pay for working at home)
prompt.prompt_jp: 「___働きかよ」

feedback.correct_en: ただ働き means working for free — Kenji grumbles that his wife is doing unpaid overtime at home.
feedback.incorrect_en: いま働き and まだ働き aren't established compounds; ただ (free, gratis) is the fixed element in this collocation.

contrast_examples.en: I was made to work for free.

prompt.context_jp: 「やっぱり ちゃーんと___しかないかな ケンカする覚悟で」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「やっぱり ちゃーんと___しかないかな ケンカする覚悟で」
prompt.prompt_en: Shoko advises Miki — choose what she suggests.

feedback.correct_en: 話し合う (discuss, talk things out mutually) fits Shoko's advice that even if a fight breaks out, Miki should discuss things with her husband.
feedback.incorrect_en: 言い張る (insist stubbornly) and 黙り込む (fall silent) are the opposite of mutual discussion, and don't match 'ケンカする覚悟で.'

prompt.context_jp: 「はい… ___といてください」(responding confidently to Saeko's request)
prompt.prompt_jp: 「はい… ___といてください」
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb completes 'Leave it to me'?

feedback.correct_en: 任せといてください (casual for 任せておいてください) is the set phrase 'leave it to me.' Sugio is confidently volunteering.
feedback.incorrect_en: 見つけ or 探し would mean 'find' or 'search,' which don't fit the confident 'leave it in my hands' context.

prompt.context_jp: 「岩崎さん ___ 押しつけてくるんだから」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「岩崎さん ___ 押しつけてくるんだから」

feedback.correct_en: 無理難題 (unreasonable/impossible demands) fits Sugio's complaint that Iwasaki keeps pushing impossible requests onto Saeko.
feedback.incorrect_en: 一石二鳥 'two birds one stone' and 自由自在 'at will' have the wrong meanings entirely.

contrast_examples.jp: 無理難題を押しつける。

prompt.context_jp: 「ここまで来てしまった以上、娘の気持ちを___しかなかった。」
prompt.prompt_jp: 「ここまで来てしまった以上、娘の気持ちを___しかなかった。」
prompt.prompt_en: Which verb best completes this sentence?

feedback.correct_en: 尊重する (respect) fits — the father realizes he must honor his daughter's wish to attend practice.
feedback.incorrect_en: 否定する (deny) and 無視する (ignore) would contradict 'having no choice but to' — those would be rejections, not resignations.

contrast_examples.jp: 子供の意思を尊重する。

prompt.context_jp: 「じゃあ___よ はい」(boss handing off a task)
prompt.prompt_jp: 「じゃあ___よ はい」
prompt.prompt_en: Choose what the boss says when assigning the job.

feedback.correct_en: 頼むよ 'I'm counting on you' is standard workplace shorthand for assigning a task.
feedback.incorrect_en: もらうよ ('I'll receive') and あげるよ ('I'll give you') don't make sense as a task handoff phrase.

contrast_examples.en: I'm counting on you for this.

prompt.context_jp: Miki is telling Shoko how her husband assumes she'll quit when he finds work.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural for Miki's complaint about her husband?

choices.text: あの人ね 私を専業主婦に戻すって発想しかないみたい
あの人ね 私が専業主婦に戻すって発想しかないみたい

feedback.correct_en: Miki is the object of 'returning to housewife' — her husband is the one doing the imagining. 私を戻す ('return me to...') correctly marks her as the one being sent back.
feedback.incorrect_en: 私が戻す would make Miki the one doing the returning (of someone else), which flips the meaning absurdly.

prompt.context_jp: Yusuke recalls how his son froze on stage last year.

choices.text: セリフ一言も言えないで突っ立ってただけだもんなあ
セリフ一言も言わないで突っ立ってただけだもんなあ

feedback.correct_en: 言えない (couldn't say) captures the child's inability — he was frozen, not refusing. The potential form matches '突っ立ってた' (standing stock-still).
feedback.incorrect_en: 言わないで (chose not to say) implies deliberate silence, but the context is a child paralyzed by stage fright.

contrast_examples.jp: 緊張して話せなかった。
contrast_examples.en: I was so nervous I couldn't speak.

prompt.context_jp: Miki hesitates about accepting the full-time job because of her husband.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural in casual spoken Japanese?

choices.text: うちの場合 旦那が問題で― 共働きをオッケーするとは…
うちの場合 旦那は問題で― 共働きをオッケーするとは…

feedback.correct_en: 旦那が問題 identifies the husband as the specific problem — exhaustive/identifying が ('the problem IS my husband'). Natural in this confessional context.
feedback.incorrect_en: 旦那は問題 sounds like topicalizing the husband and starting a general comment, but Miki is pinpointing WHAT the problem is.

prompt.context_jp: Kazuyuki reassures Miki about Rie performing Cinderella.
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds more natural as casual husband-wife reassurance?

choices.text: 大丈夫 あいつはさ 目立ちたがり屋だから
大丈夫です あの子は目立ちたがり屋ですから

feedback.correct_en: At home with his wife, Kazuyuki uses casual plain form, the rough あいつ, and filler さ. This matches an informal husband-wife chat.
feedback.incorrect_en: The です/ます version is too formal for private conversation between spouses about their own child.

prompt.context_jp: Rie, in character as the mean stepmother, scolds 'Cinderella' (her dad).
prompt.prompt_en: Which sounds like a natural bratty-stepmother line?

choices.text: サッサと掃除するんだよ
サッサと掃除をしていただけますか

feedback.correct_en: The blunt command 〜するんだよ fits the bossy stepmother role. The ending だよ and the adverb サッサと both carry impatience.
feedback.incorrect_en: していただけますか is extremely polite — it would sound ridiculous coming from a wicked stepmother ordering Cinderella around.

contrast_examples.jp: 早くやっていただけますか。
contrast_examples.en: Could you please do it quickly? (very polite)
